reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound, as it correctly links single-phase solid solution strengthening and Al/Cr surface segregation to improved strength, corrosion, and oxidation resistance, though the claim that a single-phase structure inherently yields better oxidation resistance than a multiphase one is an oversimplification that ignores the proven role of second phases in some protective scales.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with well-defined processing, comparative conditions, and a decisive falsification criterion based on statistically significant improvements in all three properties.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful for guiding alloy design, as it proposes a clear, testable processing-structure-property relationship that directly addresses the core trade-offs in lightweight HEAs for aerospace and rail applications.
